sentences.text:
Saj Food Products Private Limited vs The State Of West Bengal
& Ors on 31 January, 2025

Author: Amrita Sinha
Bench: Amrita Sinha
D/L 392
31.01.2025
Court No.14
Pradip
 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Constitutional Writ Jurisdiction
 Wpa 1887 of 2025
 Saj Food Products Private Limited
 Vs.
 The State of West Bengal & Ors.
 Mr. Abhratosh Majumdar, Sr. Adv.
 Mr. Sayan Sinha
 Mr. Nilanjan Bhattacharya
 Mr. Adil Naser
 ... for the Petitioner.

Mr. Niltpal Chatterjee
 Ms. Munmun Ganguly
 ... for the State.

Mr. Dhiraj Trivedi, Dsgi
 Mr. Arijit Majumdar
 ...for the Union of India.

Mr. Amit Mehra
 Ms. Pramita Banerjee
 Mr. Sayon Dey
 ...for the respondent nos. 3 & 4.

1 .  The prohibition order under Section 36(3) (B) of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 dated 10th January, 2025 passed by the Designated Officer (FSSAI) and DFSIO, Murshidabad is impugned in the instant writ petition.
2.

By the said order the petitioner has been directed to stop manufacturing of 'GOOGLY' biscuits,
bearing Batch No. (FTWL17C) pkg-6th July, 2024.
3.

For passing the said prohibition order, the Designated Officer relied upon the analysis report of the Food Analyst (Function) dated 18th November, 2024 mentioning that the sample does not Saj Food Products Private Limited vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 31 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66244379/
1 conform to the standard of biscuits as laid down in the Regulation No. 2.4.15.1 of FSS(FPS & FA)
due to presence of non-permitted colour (tartrazine).

entities.text: Saj Food Products Private Limited vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 31 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The sample has been held to be 'unsafe'.
4.
The petitioner challenges the jurisdiction of the Designated Officer in passing the order to stop manufacturing of the product.
It has been submitted that, the said Officer does not have the authority to direct stoppage of manufacturing of the food product.

It has also been submitted that,
the authority which conducted the food analysis does not have the accreditation to test the quality of the food colour of a food product.
5.
According to the petitioner, there is no appellate authority and as the prohibition order was passed by the Designated Officer, the appeal before the said authority will be illusory.
6. Learned counsel has referred to the report of food analysis by EFRAC in support of the submission that, tartrazine is a permitted food colour.
7. Prayer has been made to stay the operation of the impugned prohibition order.
8. According to the State respondents, the authority acted under the provisions of the Act and the corresponding Regulations to pass the said order.
The petitioner ought not to be permitted to sell any product that is unsafe and unhealthy for human consumption.

9. As it appears that, an issue of public health has cropped up in the instant writ petition, the Court is not inclined to pass any interim order staying the operation of the prohibition order immediately,
at this stage.
The Court would like to get the sample tested by the central agency.

10. Accordingly, the Designated Officer and District Food Safety Inspecting Officer, the respondent no. 7, is directed to collect fresh sample of the subject biscuit and forthwith forward the same to the National Food Laboratory at Ahinsa Khan-II, Indirapuram, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, 201014, for testing the quality of the same.

entities.text: National Food Laboratory at Ahinsa Khan-II,
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The test report shall be placed before the Court on the adjourned date.
11. The test analysis report of the National Food Laboratory shall be forwarded to the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, being the respondent no. 3, for forming an opinion.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The opinion of the respondent no. 3 shall also be placed before this Court on the adjourned date.
12. All the parties are directed to take prompt necessary steps in compliance with the directions passed hereinabove.

13. Health is of primary concern and the authorities shall ensure that, the directions passed hereinabove is complied within the prescribed time limit.
14.List the matter on 19th February, 2025.
